title: How do we find the area when the height falls outside?
description: An obtuse triangle has base six centimetres and height four centimetres, and its height lands three centimetres beyond the base. A big right triangle take away a small right triangle leaves the triangle, and the answer matches half of base times height. Keeko doubts this and takes the whole length nine as the base.
teaching_notes: One idea: when the height falls outside, the triangle is a big right triangle with a small right triangle taken away. Watch for children who use the whole stretched length as the base.

source: In an obtuse triangle ABC the height from A meets CB extended at D, with h = 4 cm, DB = 3 cm and BC = 6 cm. Find the area.
video_script.why: The child can find the area of a right triangle. Here the height falls outside the triangle, so the area comes from a big right triangle with a small one taken away.
video_script.substitution: Stretch the base to meet the height, find the big right triangle, and take away the small right triangle.
video_script.anchor: the obtuse triangle of the book, base six centimetres, height four centimetres, with the height falling outside
video_script.wrong_answer: take the whole length nine as the base
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko takes the whole stretched length nine as the base, and finds the big right triangle instead of ours. The big right triangle is larger than the triangle we want.
video_script.payoff_line: the area of the triangle is twelve square centimetres
hold_back: the area of the triangle is 12 cm²
never_show: the area of the triangle, before the answer beat
maths_rules: obtuse triangle ABC with obtuse angle at B; the height from A meets CB extended at D; AD = 4 cm, DB = 3 cm, BC = 6 cm
area of right triangle ADC = 1/2 × 9 × 4 = 18 cm²
area of right triangle ADB = 1/2 × 3 × 4 = 6 cm²
area of triangle ABC = 18 take away 6 = 12 cm²
check: 1/2 × base BC × height = 1/2 × 6 × 4 = 12 cm², the same
video_script.design: One idea: big right triangle take away small right triangle. Wrong idea: the whole stretched length is the base. The triangle stays on stage from the hook to the end. Letter names stay on screen only, and the narration says big and small right triangle.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; an obtuse triangle with base BC = 6 cm, and a dashed height of 4 cm from the top corner falling outside, to the line of the base stretched to D with DB = 3 cm

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='tri'/>A triangle has a base of six centimetres and a height of four centimetres.
<bookmark mark='out'/>The height falls outside the triangle, three centimetres beyond the base.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What is the area of the triangle?

beats.on_screen: the triangle with its outside height and the question stay on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: the base line stretches left beyond the corner to the foot of the height; a right angle is marked; the big right triangle outlines our triangle and a small right triangle

marks.stretch: the base line stretches out beyond the corner until it meets the height
marks.right: the right angle at the foot of the height is marked
marks.big: the big right triangle is outlined, holding our triangle and a small right triangle
marks.ours: the small right triangle fades and our triangle stays

beats.colours: two distinct fills for the two right triangles
narration: <bookmark mark='stretch'/>Stretch the base line out beyond the corner, until the height meets it.
<bookmark mark='right'/>They meet at a right angle, and two right triangles appear.
<bookmark mark='big'/>The big right triangle holds our triangle and a small right triangle.
<bookmark mark='ours'/>Our triangle is the big one with the small one cut away.

beats.on_screen: Given: base BC = 6 cm, height = 4 cm, DB = 3 cm
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, a triangle with base six centimetres and height four centimetres. The height lands three centimetres beyond the base.

beats.on_screen: To find: the area of the triangle

marks.find: the words to find are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the area of the triangle.

marks.len: DC = 3 + 6 = 9 cm is written along the stretched line

narration: <bookmark mark='len'/>Step one, the whole length from D to C is three plus six, which is nine centimetres.

beats.on_screen: Big right triangle: 1/2 × 9 × 4 = 18 cm². Small right triangle: 1/2 × 3 × 4 = 6 cm²

marks.big: 1/2 × 9 × 4 = 18 cm² is written beside the big right triangle
marks.small: 1/2 × 3 × 4 = 6 cm² is written beside the small right triangle

beats.colours: two distinct fills for the two right triangles
narration: <bookmark mark='big'/>Step two, the big right triangle has base nine and height four. Its area is half of four times nine, which is eighteen square centimetres.
<bookmark mark='small'/>The small right triangle has base three and height four. Its area is half of four times three, which is six.

beats.on_screen: Our triangle = big right triangle − small right triangle = 18 − 6 = 12 cm²

marks.take: the small right triangle is cut away from the big one

beats.colours: two distinct fills for the two right triangles
narration: <bookmark mark='take'/>Step four, take away the small right triangle from the big one.
<bookmark mark='calc'/>Eighteen take away six leaves twelve square centimetres.

beats.on_screen: Check: 1/2 × base × height = 1/2 × 6 × 4 = 12 cm², the same

marks.check: 1/2 × 6 × 4 = 12 cm² is written with a tick

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step five, check with the base six and height four. Half of six times four is twelve, the same area.

beats.on_screen: Answer: the area of the triangle is 12 cm²

marks.ans: the answer is boxed with its units

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The area of the triangle is twelve square centimetres.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the triangle and its outside height
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: a bubble shows the whole stretched line DC = 9 used as the base; the whole big right triangle lights up, larger than our triangle; the bubble is crossed out in the warning colour

marks.doubt: the bubble shows the whole stretched line DC = 9 used as the base
marks.big: the whole big right triangle lights up, larger than our triangle
marks.fix: the bubble is crossed out and the base 6 cm of our triangle is marked

beats.colours: warning colour on the crossed bubble
narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks we should take the whole length nine as the base.
<bookmark mark='big'/>That gives the whole big right triangle, which is larger than our triangle.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>The base of our triangle is only six, and its area is twelve square centimetres.
